content.text:
I ran 8 cold launches total (killed the process each time via force-stop, relaunched, then navigated Home → About → Diagnostics). Results:

| # | Sync status shown | Retry sync button |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sync idle | **visible** |
| 2 | Sync idle | **visible** |
| 3 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 4 | Sync idle | **visible** |
| 5 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 6 | Sync idle | **visible** |
| 7 | Sync idle | **visible** |
| 8 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |

5/8 visible (~62%), closely matching the reported "3 out of 5" pass rate.

**Root cause:** The "Retry sync" button isn't a layout/timing glitch — it's conditionally composed only when the "Sync status" field reads **"Sync idle"**; it's not rendered at all (not just hidden/disabled) when the status reads **"Sync unavailable"** (confirmed from the element dump: the button node disappears and "Run health check" shifts up to fill its place).

That status value is decided once at cold-start and then stays fixed for the rest of that process's lifetime — navigating away (About) and back to Diagnostics *without* killing the app always reproduced the same status, so it isn't re-rolled per screen visit or per recomposition.

I ruled out the obvious environmental suspects because none of them changed across any of the 8 runs while the status still flipped:
- Wi-Fi: "Wifi signal full" every time
- Battery: "Battery charging, 79 percent" every time
- Node token: constant "PHONE-NODE-742" every time
- No `ConnectivityService`/`NetworkMonitor` log activity around any launch, and the app's own About text states it "has no network access" — so it isn't a real connectivity race
- logcat shows no app-level log line at all for the sync check (no custom tag), and timestamps of process start don't show a clean parity/modulo pattern I could correlate

Given it re-rolls only on process (cold) start, is independent of every observable device/network/battery signal, and lands at a stable ~60/40 split, the most precise characterization I can give without the source is: **the Diagnostics screen seeds its "Sync status" from a non-deterministic value generated once at app/process startup (e.g., an unseeded `Random`/`nanoTime`-derived coin flip) rather than from any real device or network state.** That's the flake source — the test should either seed/mock that sync-status provider to a fixed value, or assert on both the "idle" and "unavailable" branches instead of assuming the button is always present.
